albums.blurb: El Michels Affair is the studio outfit of New York multi-instrumentalist and producer Leon Michels, assembled from session players in the Daptone/Truth & Soul orbit; Michels went on to co-found Big Crown Records and produce for artists from Lee Fields to Norah Jones. Sounding Out the City, the band's 2005 debut and the first full-length on the Truth & Soul label, is a fully instrumental record in the style Michels dubbed 'cinematic soul' — gritty soul and funk grooves that draw on library music, afrobeat, and the raw recording aesthetic of early reggae. Eleven tracks in 34 minutes, with no vocals anywhere on the album.
albums.reception: AllMusic's biography of the band records that the debut earned critical acclaim in the deep-funk scene, and its success led the group to back Raekwon and other Wu-Tang Clan members on stage — the collaboration that produced 2009's Enter the 37th Chamber.

albums.blurb: Is This It is the debut album by the New York five-piece led by Julian Casablancas, recorded with producer Gordon Raphael in a Lower East Side basement studio and released in July 2001. Its deliberately dry, compressed sound — Casablancas' voice run through an amp over interlocking Albert Hammond Jr. and Nick Valensi guitar lines — became the template for the decade's garage rock revival, and the record stands as the band's defining statement, with every later Strokes album measured against it. The US edition swapped 'New York City Cops' for 'When It Started' in the wake of September 11.
albums.reception: NME named Is This It the greatest album of the 2000s in its 2009 end-of-decade list, and the album has been certified platinum by the RIAA in the United States.

albums.blurb: Alice Coltrane was a Detroit-born pianist and harpist who played in John Coltrane's final groups and, after his death in 1967, built one of the most distinctive catalogs in jazz. Journey in Satchidananda, her fourth album, released on Impulse! in February 1971 and named for her guru Swami Satchidananda, sets Pharoah Sanders' soprano saxophone and her own cascading harp over modal bass vamps and the drone of the Indian tanpura. It is the centerpiece of her early-70s spiritual jazz run and a documented influence on later artists from Radiohead to her grandnephew Flying Lotus.
albums.reception: Journey in Satchidananda was ranked number 446 on Rolling Stone's 2020 edition of the 500 Greatest Albums of All Time.
